claim_text: The project involves actions and agreements with local communities and authorities to implement management plans and safeguard measures, which could be affected by future policy changes.

metadata.supporting_text: The proponents, who hold the right to the land, have implemented projects, agreements and contracts executed within the project area (the data has been provided to the DOE), in association with public, private, and mixed entities, with different participation mechanisms depending on the capacities of the parties. These actions have ensured that climate addi- tionality is achieved by reducing greenhouse gas emissions, framed by the United Nations Framework Commission on Climate Change (UNFCCC). In the first place, there is the formu- lation of the cultural and environmental management plan for the Reserve, which the re- serve implements and develops through the support of the local FUNAI office. With this, a recognition of t he problems related to the environmental aspect and quality of life. This defines certain actions that have contributed to the loss of habitats, such as the extraction of wood with chainsaws, crops for illicit use, hunting, fishing, and poor garbage manage- ment. With this exercise, certain agreements were proposed between the inhabitants of the reservation and five projects were prioritized to improve the situation that they had identified at the time.

claim_text: The project is located in an area with human activity and land use that could be affected by extreme weather or natural disasters, such as droughts or floods, which are common in semi-arid regions with negative water balance.

metadata.supporting_text: The Fortín Paunero Establishment is situated in the southwest of Buenos Aires Province, Argentina, in the Sandy Pampa subregion, spanning 2,333 hectares. This semi-arid region experiences an average annual temperature of 14°C and receives around 800 mm of rain annually, while potential evapotranspiration reaches 1,200 mm, resulting in a negative water balance (Oyarzabal et al., 2018). The area’s natural vegetation consists primarily of steppe and pseudo-steppe grasslands, along with various other types such as shrubs and rush beds, dominated by genera like Stipa, Poa, and Bromus (Oyarzabal et al., 2018). Human activity, mainly agricultural expansion, has significantly altered the natural environment.
